summary: 10 checked, 9 keep, 1 reject. All licences re-read from the Commons API on 2026-11-24; both CC BY 2.0 Flickr photos were also confirmed on Flickr itself. Rejected: semper-augustus-tulip-book-six (a Rijksmuseum press photograph of a 3D open book; the public-domain tags cover only the drawing). Four files (brueghel, ward, leyster, receipt) are resampled Commons renditions, not the original bytes, though pixel sizes match. Strongest for large use: tulip-backlit-dark-background (true black negative space), pot-floras-wagon-of-fools, brueghel, hogarth, ward (needs a levels stretch), tulip-field-rows-holland. The two CC BY photos need visible credit and a note that they were converted to grayscale.

items.whatItShows: Oil on panel, c. 1640-1650: monkeys dressed as tulip dealers in a vaulted hall. Left: banquet table with white cloth, a carved fireplace/buffet with a framed painting and a vase of tulips above it. Centre: a line of standing monkeys negotiating, reading a list, shaking hands, one seated writing. Right: money-counting table at a pillar, a fight with a sword, then an open arcade onto a tree-lined landscape with small figures and a white horse. Cut tulips lie on the floor at bottom centre-right.
items.subjectRegion: Figures form a horizontal frieze across the lower half (roughly y 55-95%), densest at lower left (banquet) and centre. Brightest accents: white tablecloth at far left edge (y 75-88%), sky in the upper right quadrant.
items.negativeSpace: Upper left quarter is a large plain mid-dark brick wall (x 0-35%, y 0-45%) apart from the framed picture; upper centre is the dark vault. Floor at bottom right corner is a quiet mid-grey. No true black area; text here needs a scrim.
items.depthStructure: Three clear layers: foreground monkeys and tulips on the floor; middle ground back wall with table, doorway and pictures (centre, x 37-58%); far background landscape through the arcade on the right third. The left wall and vault recede steeply to a vanishing area around x 55%, y 45%, so depth separation should be strong.
items.tonalNotes: Mid-key and fairly dark overall (median about 80/255). Blacks in the monkeys coats and fireplace recess; highlights in tablecloth, ruffs, tulips on the floor and the sky at right. Fine craquelure visible at full size, reads as texture.
items.cropAdvice: Native 1.45:1. Crops well to 16:9 by trimming top vault. A left-two-thirds crop gives a pure interior; the right third alone gives pillar plus landscape. Do not crop the bottom: the cut tulips are the key motif.
items.attribution: Jan Brueghel the Younger, Allegory of Tulipomania, c. 1640-1650. Image: Dorotheum, via Wikimedia Commons. Public domain.

items.whatItShows: Oil on panel, c. 1637: a sail-driven land wagon on a beach. Flora sits high at the rear (left) holding bunches of tulips under a large flag painted with tulips; below her men in fools caps decorated with tulips drink and weigh money; two women sit at the front (right), one reaching out towards a bird flying away. A crowd of Haarlem weavers follows on the left; a church skyline on the left horizon; a second wagon founders in the sea at far right.
items.subjectRegion: Wagon and figures fill the centre, x 22-85%, y 15-95%; mast and sail are the vertical axis at about x 50%, topped by a pennant reaching to x 72% at y 5-12%. Flora (the lightest figure) at x 25-40%, y 40-65%. Crowd at far left edge x 0-22%, y 65-100%.
items.negativeSpace: Sky: upper left corner (x 0-18%, y 0-50%) and the whole upper right (x 62-100%, y 0-50%) are smooth pale-to-mid grey, only a small bird at x 85-92%, y 48-55%. Sand at the bottom right corner is an empty mid-grey. These are light areas: use dark text or a scrim.
items.depthStructure: Foreground: wagon, wheels, crowd and debris on the sand. Middle: flag and sail standing against the sky. Background: flat horizon at about y 70% with church skyline (left) and sea with the sinking wagon (right). Dark figures against a pale sky give a clean silhouette edge, so separation between wagon and sky is very strong; little depth within the figure group itself.
items.tonalNotes: Balanced mid-key (median about 129). Blacks in the dark costumes at centre and the woman in black at lower left; highlights in Flora, tulips, collars, pennant and the horizon band of sky. Sky is a smooth gradient, darker at top.
items.cropAdvice: Native 1.37:1. For 16:9 trim the top sky down to just above the pennant and a little sand; keep both wheels. The right 40% (women, bird, sinking wagon, empty sky) works as a quieter secondary crop.
items.attribution: Hendrik Gerritsz Pot, Flora's Wagon of Fools, c. 1637. Frans Hals Museum, Haarlem. Image: Google Arts & Culture, via Wikimedia Commons. Public domain.

items.whatItShows: Etching and engraving, 1721, full sheet. A London square packed with a crowd; at centre a merry-go-round on a pole topped by a goat and a sign "Who'l Ride", carrying speculators on wooden horses. Left: a building with a balcony full of women, a clock, a devil hacking at Fortune in a shop front, and three clergymen gambling on the ground. Right: the base of the Monument with a re-cut inscription about the South Sea in 1720, foxes on its ledge, a man being flogged, and in front Honesty broken on a wheel. St Paul's dome in the distance. Four columns of engraved verse fill a strip below the image.
items.subjectRegion: Image area occupies y 0-85%; verse strip y 86-100%. Merry-go-round at x 37-68%, y 22-60%. Crowd band across x 20-75%, y 52-78%. Wheel with naked figure at x 48-70%, y 70-80%. Monument block is a large mass at x 73-98%, y 0-75%. Devil and building at x 0-33%.
items.negativeSpace: No dark quiet area. Lightest/quietest zones: the clouds at upper centre (x 37-72%, y 3-25%) and the pale paved ground at lower centre-left (x 28-48%, y 78-84%). The Monument face (x 78-95%, y 28-55%) is an even mid-grey hatched panel carrying its own inscription. Everything else is busy line work.
items.depthStructure: Stage-like: foreground figures (gamblers lower left, wheel centre, flogging right); middle crowd and merry-go-round; background buildings and dome at x 60-75%, y 35-50%; sky. The two flanking architectural masses act as wings. As a line engraving the depth cue comes from hatching density, not tone gradients, so expect an estimated depth map to be noisy; best rendered as layered planes.
items.tonalNotes: Pure black line on warm pale paper (reads light grey, about 170-227). Densest blacks in the left building shadows and the crowd. Already monochrome; in grayscale you may want to lift the paper to white or invert for a dark layout (inversion works well with line engravings).
items.cropAdvice: Native 1.25:1 including verses. Crop off the bottom 15% to lose the verse strip and get roughly 1.47:1 image only. A central crop x 25-75% isolates the merry-go-round and crowd.
items.attribution: William Hogarth, The South Sea Scheme, 1721, etching and engraving. National Gallery of Art, Washington, via Wikimedia Commons. CC0 1.0.

items.reason: Licence confirmed public domain: Edward Matthew Ward died 1879 and this is a 19th-century steel engraving after his 1847 painting, so both the design and the engraving are long out of copyright. Caveat: the Commons page is poorly documented (it labels the file as the Tate painting and names no engraver or date; source is a Harvard Business School Baker Library web page), but nothing about the object allows a subsisting copyright. Local file is a resampled rendition at the native 2239x1510 (SHA-1 differs from the Commons original), still above the 1400 px floor. Slightly low-contrast scan; fix with levels.

items.whatItShows: Steel engraving after E. M. Ward's painting: Change Alley, London, 1720, crowded with speculators. Left: a pawnbroker and jeweller's shop with three balls sign, a woman pawning jewels at the counter, and a ruined man and woman crouching in the bottom-left corner. Centre: a man seen from behind in a long coat and wig reads a paper to two fashionable women, a boy tugging at him, a small dog. Right: a clerk writing at a table surrounded by eager buyers, a man standing on a raised box above them, a doorway with a lion knocker. Background: the facade of Garraway's coffee house with people at the windows, an arch signed "Change Alley" and a placard "South Sea Stock".
items.subjectRegion: Figures fill the whole width in the band y 40-95%. Central standing man (back view) at x 38-50%, y 45-95% is the anchor. Right-hand group around the table x 67-100%, y 30-100%. Crouching pair bottom-left x 0-15%, y 75-100%. Garraway's facade x 38-72%, y 0-45%.
items.negativeSpace: Top-left corner (shop upper storey, x 0-28%, y 0-28%) is dark, low-detail timber. The paved ground at bottom centre (x 28-65%, y 88-100%) is an even mid-grey with a few scraps of paper. Top-right corner is a dark awning. No clean empty area; a gradient scrim at top or bottom is needed for text.
items.depthStructure: Deep street scene: foreground figures at left, centre and right; a dense middle-ground crowd of heads at y 40-55%; background facade and the archway at x 60-70%, y 28-45% opening to a lighter street with a coach. Buildings on both sides funnel towards that arch, so depth separation is good and well suited to a depth map.
items.tonalNotes: Dark, compressed range (2nd-98th percentile about 29-178, median 77): no true white, highlights are light grey (womens dresses, bonnets, the paper being read, the lit facade). Blacks in coats, the crouching figures and the right-hand group. Needs a levels stretch; after that it has a rich photographic-looking tonal scale.
items.cropAdvice: Native 1.48:1. Trims to 16:9 by losing some of the top facade. Centre crop x 28-68% isolates the reader and two women with Garraway's behind; the right third alone (clerk at table) also stands on its own.
items.attribution: After Edward Matthew Ward, The South Sea Bubble, a Scene in 'Change Alley in 1720, 19th-century engraving after the painting of 1847. Scan: Baker Library, Harvard Business School, via Wikimedia Commons. Public domain.

items.reason: Licence confirmed public domain (c. 1643 watercolour, PD-Art). Genuine tulip-book sheet, no watermark or border. Local file is a resampled rendition at the native size (SHA-1 differs from the Commons original). Do not credit the sheet to Judith Leyster: Commons states only folios 29 and 30 are hers.

items.whatItShows: Watercolour on paper/vellum, c. 1643: a single flamed ("broken") tulip, red-and-white in the original, with a long straight stem and two leaves, one large leaf curling out to the lower left and one rising to the right. Plain light sheet, slightly cockled. Sheet edge cuts a faint inscription at the very bottom.
items.subjectRegion: Vertical, slightly left of centre. Bloom at x 34-70%, y 4-30%; stem down the line x 50%; leaves fill x 22-74%, y 40-97%.
items.negativeSpace: Everything around the plant is empty light paper: full-height margins at left (x 0-22%) and right (x 75-100%), and the areas either side of the stem at y 30-45%. All light (about 230/255); usable behind dark text, or invert the image for a dark layout.
items.depthStructure: None in the picture: one flat subject on a flat sheet. Any depth must be synthetic (the plant lifted off the paper as a single layer). Faint paper undulation gives a little texture.
items.tonalNotes: High-key: paper at 230-245, flame markings and leaf shadows down to about 60; no deep black. In grayscale the red flames become dark streaks on white petals, which reads well. Mask or invert to make it sit on black.
items.cropAdvice: Native 0.75:1 portrait. Crop to the bloom alone (top 32%) for a square detail; the full plant needs a tall slot. Trim the bottom 2% to remove the clipped inscription.
items.attribution: Unknown artist, tulip from the Tulip Book associated with Judith Leyster, c. 1643. Frans Hals Museum, Haarlem, via Wikimedia Commons. Public domain.

items.reason: Licence not confirmable for this file. The Commons tags (PD-old-100, PD-US-expired) only cover the 17th-century drawing. The file itself is a modern photograph of a three-dimensional object (open bound book with page block, gutter, ribbon markers and cast shadows), taken from a Rijksmuseum press release, with no photographer named and no licence statement from the museum. That is a press photo with an unlicensed photographic layer, which the brief excludes. Image quality is fine; the rejection is on rights only. If this motif is wanted, source a flat reproduction instead: Commons lists a cropped derivative "Semper Augustus - Six Collection (no book).jpg" (still derived from the same press photo, so check it separately), or use the well-documented anonymous Semper Augustus gouache (Norton Simon Museum) file on Commons.

items.subjectRegion: Tulip on the page, centre: bloom x 25-62%, y 15-48%; stem at x 50%, y 48-95%; inscription x 57-85%, y 82-90%. Page block and ribbons at x 85-97%.
items.negativeSpace: Light page around the bloom (upper left and upper right of the page); grey shadow band along the bottom 8% of the frame.

items.whatItShows: Trompe-l'oeil medley engraving (portrait), titled at the top "The Bubblers Medley, or a Sketch of the Times: Being Europes Memorial for the Year 1720". Overlapping, tilted sheets as if scattered on a table: top-left "The Dutch Bubblers" (men in a street, with verse); top-right a coffee-house interior ("Mint Coffe House") with speech banners; centre a tilted crowd scene "Quinquempoix Street"; left a court playing card (knave of hearts); lower left "Bubble Poem" with a scene of gentlemen and two columns of verse; lower centre a page of "The London Gazette" dated August 1720; right a tilted card "Stock-Jobbing Cards, or the Humours of Change Alley"; bottom-right a putto blowing soap bubbles, with the publisher's line "Printed for Carington Bowles".
items.subjectRegion: Fills the whole sheet edge to edge inside a narrow pale margin (about 3% each side). Title banner y 5-12%. Darkest, most pictorial block is the Quinquempoix Street print at x 35-90%, y 37-62%. Playing card at x 7-27%, y 45-73%. Putto at x 80-93%, y 80-93%.
items.negativeSpace: None. The only calm areas are text blocks (verse lower left x 7-45%, y 76-97%; Gazette x 45-72%, y 62-95%), which are light with fine lettering. The outer sheet margin is plain light grey.
items.depthStructure: Depicted depth is shallow by design: about four or five overlapping paper layers with engraved drop shadows on a hatched ground. Ideal for a layered-planes treatment (each sheet as its own plane); an automatic depth map will be unreliable.
items.tonalNotes: Black line on greyish paper (paper about 187-221, lines down to about 32). Overall mid-light with dark concentrations in the centre print, the top-left print and the lower-left scene. The sheet tone is a little dull; lift the paper with levels or invert.
items.cropAdvice: Native 0.75:1 portrait. Good detail crops: the playing card; the Quinquempoix Street crowd (rotate about 15 degrees to level it); the putto with bubbles at bottom right (a literal bubble motif); the title banner as a wide strip.
items.attribution: Anonymous, The Bubblers Medley, or a Sketch of the Times, design of 1720 (impression c. 1766-1793). Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam, RP-P-1905-6516, via Wikimedia Commons. CC0 1.0.

items.whatItShows: Scan of a part-printed, part-handwritten South Sea Company transfer receipt: "London, the 22 Day of June 1720. Received of Robert Surman Esq. the Sum of four thousand pounds being in full for One thousand pounds in the Capital and Principal Stock of The Governour and Company of Merchants of Great-Britain, Trading to the South-Seas...", with a bracket and "4000" at right, a number "(484)", large flourished signatures along the bottom (witness at left, "Gerard Van Neck" at centre), a torn notch at the upper left edge and a few stains.
items.subjectRegion: The document fills the frame edge to edge. Printed text block x 8-78%, y 8-60%. Large drop-cap R at x 9-14%, y 18-30%. Signatures across the bottom y 62-98%, the heaviest ink at lower left (x 12-40%, y 72-95%).
items.negativeSpace: Right-hand quarter (x 80-100%) is mostly blank paper with only a tick, "4000" and "(484)". Upper right corner x 82-100%, y 15-40% is the emptiest patch. All light paper; no dark area.
items.depthStructure: None: a flat sheet. Paper texture, creases and ink give surface relief only. Treat as a single plane, perhaps tilted in 3D.
items.tonalNotes: High-key: paper about 205-215, ink near black, surround pure white (255). Very strong ink-on-paper contrast. Invert or mask the white surround for a dark layout.
items.cropAdvice: Native 1.89:1, already a wide strip. Detail crops: the handwritten "four thousand pounds" lines (x 25-78%, y 10-38%); the signatures; the words "Trading to the South-Seas" (x 8-55%, y 44-52%).
items.attribution: South Sea Company stock transfer receipt, London, 22 June 1720. Photo: Julie Ceccaldi, Sammlung Commodore (Ruediger K. Weng), via Wikimedia Commons. CC0 1.0.

items.whatItShows: Photograph: one open tulip, side-lit by hard sunlight, on a pure black background, leaning to the right on a diagonal stem. Shadows of the petals fall across each other. At lower left, in deep shadow, a closed bud and several pointed leaf blades are just rim-lit.
items.subjectRegion: Bloom at centre-right: x 48-88%, y 27-90%, about 60% of frame height. Stem enters from the bottom at x 46-56%. Dim bud and leaves at x 0-42%, y 30-100%.
items.negativeSpace: Excellent: the whole top band (y 0-25%, full width) is true black, the upper left quadrant is black apart from the faint leaf tip at x 28%, and the right edge strip (x 88-100%) is black. Median pixel value is 1/255. Text can sit directly on the image at top left, top right or far right.
items.depthStructure: Two layers on a void: the lit bloom in front, the shadowed bud and leaves slightly behind and to the left, then black. Within the bloom the overlapping petals give real volumetric relief. Ideal for a point cloud: the black drops out to nothing and the petals form a clean 3D shell.
items.tonalNotes: Extreme low-key: over half the frame at 0-1, highlights up to about 230 on the sunlit petals, with soft mid-greys where petal shadows fall. Nothing to fix; do not lift the blacks.
items.cropAdvice: Native 1.5:1. Works at 16:9 or wider by trimming top black. For a portrait slot crop x 42-95%. Can be flipped horizontally if the layout needs the flower on the left (allowed under CC BY; mention adaptation).

items.whatItShows: Landscape photograph in low sun: a Dutch bulb field with planted rows and a rutted dirt track converging towards a distant tree line, a stand of tall bare trees on the left, a heavy clouded sky, and in the right foreground a grassy bank dropping to a canal with three swans on the water and reeds reflected.
items.subjectRegion: Field rows fan from the left edge to a vanishing point at about x 65%, y 37%. Track curves from bottom left to that point. Tall trees at x 0-45%, y 10-33%. Grass bank is the dark mass at x 0-90%, y 65-88%. Swans are tiny at x 85-95%, y 39-41%. Horizon at y 33-37%.
items.negativeSpace: Water at the right edge and bottom right (x 82-100%, y 38-100%) is smooth light grey; water strip along the bottom (y 90-100%) is mid-dark and calm. The grass bank (x 0-55%, y 68-85%) is the darkest calm area and the best place for light text. Sky is light and busy with cloud.
items.depthStructure: Strong, continuous recession: foreground reeds, bank and water; middle ground rows and track running to the vanishing point; background tree line; then sky. One of the best images in the set for real depth, with a ground plane that will reconstruct cleanly.
items.tonalNotes: Full range (about 12-230, median 110). Blacks in the tree line and the shadowed bank; highlights in cloud edges, the lit field at far left and the water at right. Good contrast without adjustment.
items.cropAdvice: Native 1.5:1. For 16:9 or 21:9 trim sky from the top, keeping the horizon in the upper third. Cropping to x 0-80% removes the canal and makes it a pure field image.
items.attribution: Photo: rboed* (Flickr), "Tulip field in Holland", 2021, via Wikimedia Commons. CC BY 2.0. Converted to grayscale.
